ei.title: 8번: The Unavoidable Consequences of Our Actions
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: The concept of karma suggests that every action has a consequence, whether in this life or the next. Essentially, karma is like a seed; what you plant, you will eventually harvest. For example, a man kept harassing others online under the cloak of anonymity. Eventually, however, his identity was exposed and legal action was taken against him. In a different instance, a CEO of a large company paid the necessary, expensive fees to dispose of waste from its factory correctly, while her rivals simply dumped their waste from their factories into local rivers. A government investigation later revealed the behavior of her competitors. They were forced to pay massive fines and eventually went bankrupt. These examples remind us that living a moral life matters, even if we don't immediately see the results of our actions.

questions.passage: The concept of karma suggests that every action has a consequence, whether in this life or the next. Essentially, karma is like a seed; what you plant, you will eventually (A)[harvest / waste]. For example, a man kept harassing others online under the cloak of anonymity. Eventually, however, his identity was (B)[exposed / hidden] and legal action was taken against him. In a different instance, a CEO of a large company paid the necessary, expensive fees to dispose of waste from its factory correctly, while her rivals simply dumped their waste from their factories into local rivers. A government investigation later revealed the behavior of her competitors. They were forced to pay massive fines and eventually went (C)[bankrupt / wealthy]. These examples remind us that living a moral life matters, even if we don't immediately see the results of our actions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) harvest=거두다 / waste=낭비하다 (B) exposed=드러난 / hidden=숨겨진 (C) bankrupt=파산한 / wealthy=부유한
det.analysis:
① harvest — exposed — bankrupt: 심은 대로 '거두고(harvest)', 신원이 '드러났으며(exposed)', 결국 '파산했다(bankrupt)' ←정답
② waste: '심은 것을 낭비한다'는 씨앗 비유와 안 맞음
③ hidden/wealthy: 신원이 '숨겨졌다'/'부유해졌다'는 처벌 흐름과 반대
④ waste/hidden: 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 심은 대로 harvest(거두다), 신원 exposed(드러남), 처벌로 bankrupt(파산)

For example, a man kept harassing others online under the cloak of anonymity. Eventually, however, his identity was exposed and legal action was taken against him. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) dispose=처리하다 / increase=늘리다 (B) revealed=밝혔다 / hid=숨겼다 (C) bankrupt=파산한 / wealthy=부유한
det.analysis:
① increase: 폐기물을 '늘리려고' 비용을 낸다? 오히려 '처리하려고(dispose)' 낸 것
② hid/wealthy: 조사가 '숨겼다'? 경쟁사가 '부유해졌다'? 처벌 흐름과 반대
③ dispose — revealed — bankrupt: 폐기물을 '처리하고', 조사가 '밝혔으며', 경쟁사가 '파산했다' ←정답
④ increase/hid: 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 폐기물을 dispose(처리), 조사가 revealed(밝힘), 경쟁사 bankrupt(파산)

questions.passage: The concept of karma suggests that every action has a consequence, whether in this life or the next. Essentially, karma is like a seed; what you plant, you will eventually harvest. For example, a man kept harassing others online under the cloak of anonymity. Eventually, however, his identity was exposed and legal action was taken against him. In a different instance, a CEO of a large company (A)[paid / saved] the necessary, expensive fees to dispose of waste from its factory correctly, while her rivals simply dumped their waste from their factories into local rivers. A government investigation later revealed the behavior of her competitors. They were forced to pay (B)[massive / minor] fines and eventually went bankrupt. These examples remind us that living a (C)[moral / selfish] life matters, even if we don't immediately see the results of our actions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) paid=지불했다 / saved=아꼈다 (B) massive=막대한 / minor=사소한 (C) moral=도덕적인 / selfish=이기적인
det.analysis:
① saved: CEO가 비용을 '아꼈다'? 폐기물을 제대로 처리하려 비용을 '지불했다(paid)'
② paid — massive — moral: CEO가 비용을 '지불하고', 경쟁사는 '막대한' 벌금을 물었으며, '도덕적' 삶이 중요하다 ←정답
③ saved/minor/selfish: 문맥과 반대
④ minor/selfish: '사소한' 벌금? '이기적인' 삶이 중요? 문맥과 반대
det.tip: CEO는 비용을 paid(지불), 경쟁사는 massive(막대한) 벌금, moral(도덕적) 삶 강조

questions.passage: The concept of karma suggests that every action has a consequence, whether in this life or the next. Essentially, karma is like a seed; what you plant, you will eventually ①<u>harvest</u>. For example, a man kept harassing others online under the cloak of anonymity. Eventually, however, his identity was ②<u>exposed</u> and legal action was taken against him. In a different instance, a CEO of a large company paid the necessary, expensive fees to dispose of waste from its factory correctly, while her rivals simply dumped their waste from their factories into local rivers. A government investigation later revealed the behavior of her competitors. They were ③<u>allowed</u> to pay massive fines and eventually went bankrupt. These examples remind us that living a ④<u>moral</u> life matters, even if we don't immediately see the results of our actions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ allowed → forced: 경쟁사들은 벌금을 물도록 '강요받았다(forced)'. '허용받았다(allowed)'는 정반대
det.analysis:
① harvest: 심은 대로 '거둔다' — 적절
② exposed: 신원이 '드러났다' — 적절
③ allowed: 경쟁사들은 잘못이 드러나 벌금을 물도록 '강요받은(forced)' 거예요. '허용받았다(allowed)'는 처벌 상황과 정반대라 부적절 ←정답
④ moral: '도덕적인' 삶 — 적절
det.tip: 처벌로 벌금을 물도록 forced(강요받음). allowed(허용)는 반대

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② helping → harassing: 남자는 남을 '괴롭혔고(harassing)' 그래서 법적 조치를 받았다. '도왔다(helping)'는 모순
det.analysis:
① harvest: 심은 대로 '거둔다' — 적절
② helping: 남자가 사람들을 '돕다가' 신원이 드러나 법적 조치를 받는다? 앞뒤가 안 맞아요. 남을 '괴롭혔기(harassing)' 때문에 처벌받은 거라 helping은 부적절 ←정답
③ paid: CEO가 비용을 '지불했다' — 적절
④ bankrupt: 경쟁사들이 '파산했다' — 적절
det.tip: 법적 조치를 받은 이유 = 남을 harassing(괴롭힘). helping(도움)은 모순

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ physical → moral: 글의 교훈은 '도덕적인(moral)' 삶이 중요하다는 것. '육체적인(physical)'은 무관
det.analysis:
① harassing: 남을 '괴롭혔다' — 적절
② paid: 비용을 '지불했다' — 적절
③ bankrupt: '파산했다' — 적절
④ physical: 글 전체는 착하게 살면 좋은 결과가 온다는 이야기라, '도덕적인(moral)' 삶이 중요하다고 해야 맞아요. '육체적인(physical)' 삶은 주제와 무관해 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 글의 교훈 = moral(도덕적인) 삶의 중요성. physical(육체적)은 무관

questions.passage:

(B) After resting for a few days, she said she felt completely <u>fine</u> and was ready to return to work.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 fine의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: fine: (A) 벌금(명사) (B) 건강한, 괜찮은(형용사)
det.analysis:
① (A) 벌금 (B) 건강한: 법을 어겨 정부에 낸 것은 '벌금(fine)', 며칠 쉬고 나서 '괜찮다(fine)'고 느낌 ←정답
② (A) 건강한 (B) 벌금: 의미가 뒤바뀜
③ (A) 벌금 (B) 미세한: (B)에서 '미세한'은 문맥 부적절
④ (A) 좋은 날씨 (B) 건강한: (A)는 날씨 이야기가 아님
det.tip: fine의 다의어: 벌금(명사) vs 건강한·괜찮은(형용사)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the situation in which someone's name or identity is not known"

det.analysis:
① identity(신원): 이름이 '알려진' 상태라 정의와 반대
② authority(권위): 정의와 무관
③ publicity(널리 알려짐): 이름이 알려지는 것이라 반대
④ anonymity(익명): 이름이나 신원이 알려지지 않은 상태 ←정답
det.tip: name or identity is not known(이름·신원이 알려지지 않음) → anonymity(익명)

questions.passage: In a different instance, a CEO of a large company paid the necessary, expensive fees to dispose of waste from its factory __________ (correct), while her rivals simply dumped their waste from their factories into local rivers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: correct(형용사: 올바른) → correctly(부사: 올바르게). 동사 dispose를 꾸미는 부사
det.analysis: correct(형용사)를 부사 correctly로 바꿔요. 'dispose of waste ___(폐기물을 ~하게 처리하다)'에서 동사 dispose를 꾸미는 자리라 부사가 필요해요. 'dispose ... correctly(올바르게 처리하다)'가 맞아요
det.tip: 동사(dispose)를 꾸미는 자리 = 부사. correct + -ly → correctly

questions.passage: A government investigation later revealed the behavior of her competitors. They were forced to pay __________ (mass) fines and eventually went bankrupt.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: mass(명사: 덩어리, 다량) → massive(형용사: 막대한). 명사 fines를 꾸미는 형용사
det.analysis: mass(명사)를 형용사 massive로 바꿔요. 뒤의 명사 fines(벌금)를 꾸미는 자리라 형용사가 필요해요. 'massive fines(막대한 벌금)'가 맞아요
det.tip: 명사(fines)를 꾸미는 자리 = 형용사. mass → massive(막대한)

questions.passage: The concept of karma suggests that every action has a consequence, whether in this life or the next. Essentially, karma is like a seed; what you plant, you will eventually harvest. For example, a man kept harassing others online under the cloak of anonymity. Eventually, however, his identity was exposed and __________ was taken against him. In a different instance, a CEO of a large company paid the necessary, expensive fees to dispose of waste from its factory correctly, while her rivals simply dumped their waste from their factories into local rivers. A government investigation later revealed the behavior of her competitors. They were forced to pay massive fines and eventually went bankrupt. These examples remind us that living a moral life matters, even if we don't immediately see the results of our actions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: legal action=법적 조치 / a moral seed=도덕적인 씨앗 / massive waste=막대한 폐기물 / the next life=다음 생
det.analysis:
① legal action(법적 조치): 익명 뒤에 숨어 남을 괴롭힌 남자의 신원이 드러나 그에게 '법적 조치'가 취해짐 ←정답
② a moral seed(도덕적인 씨앗): 문맥 부적절
③ massive waste(막대한 폐기물): 다른 사례의 단어 조합
④ the next life(다음 생): 앞 문장의 단어이나 이 자리엔 부적절
det.tip: identity was exposed and ___ was taken against him → legal action(법적 조치)

questions.passage: The concept of karma suggests that every action has a consequence, whether in this life or the next. Essentially, karma is like a seed; what you plant, you will eventually harvest. For example, a man kept harassing others online under the cloak of anonymity. Eventually, however, his identity was exposed and legal action was taken against him. In a different instance, a CEO of a large company paid the necessary, expensive fees to dispose of waste from its factory correctly, while her rivals simply dumped their waste from their factories __________. A government investigation later revealed the behavior of her competitors. They were forced to pay massive fines and eventually went bankrupt. These examples remind us that living a moral life matters, even if we don't immediately see the results of our actions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 익명이라는 장막 뒤에서 / 공장에서 올바르게 / 지역 하천으로 / 이생 또는 다음 생에
det.analysis:
① under the cloak of anonymity(익명이라는 장막 뒤에서): 다른 사례(온라인 괴롭힘)의 표현
② from its factory correctly(공장에서 올바르게): CEO가 '올바르게 처리한' 쪽의 표현이라 경쟁사 행동과 반대
③ into local rivers(지역 하천으로): 경쟁사들이 폐기물을 그냥 '지역 하천에' 버렸다 ←정답
④ in this life or the next(이생 또는 다음 생에): 첫 문장의 표현이라 이 자리엔 부적절
det.tip: her rivals simply dumped their waste ... ___ → into local rivers(지역 하천으로)

ch: in this life or the next
